extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians considering submitting manuscripts to the Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society (authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Information and high-level submission standards for authors who wish to publish research articles in the Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society, including scope, peer-review model, open-access options, and production steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishes articles of the highest quality and significance across a broad range of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should submit work that constitutes a significant advance in mathematical knowledge; the journal is the Society’s high-impact flagship and seeks papers of the highest quality and significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope (broad range of mathematics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal publishes articles across a broad range of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure their manuscript fits general-interest high-quality mathematics rather than specialist-only work; related specialist journals (Bulletin, Journal, Transactions, Journal of Topology) may be more appropriate for specialist or differently-formatted contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No page length restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no page length restrictions for submitted papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are not constrained by a maximum page limit when preparing submissions for the Proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles published in this journal are peer reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts will undergo peer review as part of the editorial process; however, editors retain the right to reject papers without sending them for external review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial desk rejection policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors may reject papers without external review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before external refereeing, an editor may assess suitability and quality and can decide to reject; authors should read submission guidelines and ensure fit and quality to avoid desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity transparency / anonymization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal uses a single-anonymised review model (authors anonymised to reviewers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer interaction and review record publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer interacts with: Editor. Review information published: None.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers communicate via the handling editor; the journal does not publish peer-review reports or review histories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access model and funder compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proceedings is a hybrid open access journal with options for gold and green open access publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By default articles are subscription-based; authors with funder/institution open-access requirements should check compliant routes and contact the journal team if they cannot identify a compliant route. See the journal's open access page for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production / typesetting after acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper is accepted it will be sent to the publisher for typesetting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be prepared for publisher-led production steps post-acceptance and may contact the LMS or Wiley teams depending on production status (contact details provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal-fit guidance and related publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Related journals publish specialist or different-length articles (Bulletin, Journal, Transactions, Journal of Topology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consider whether their submission is better suited to a specialist journal (e.g., concise advances or surveys to Bulletin, longer reports to Journal, fully open-access Transactions) and choose the appropriate LMS journal.
